assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Conjugate acid–base pair
items.clue: Two species that differ by exactly one proton (H⁺).

items.label: Brønsted–Lowry acid
items.clue: A species that donates a proton (H⁺) to another species.

items.label: Ion product constant of water
items.clue: Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻], which has the value 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K.

items.label: Neutralization
items.clue: The reaction of an acid with a base to give a salt and water.

questions.stem:
Ammonia reacts with water:
NH₃(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
Which species acts as a Brønsted–Lowry acid in the forward reaction?

options.text: NH₃, as it gains a proton to form NH₄⁺
OH⁻, as it forms when H₂O loses a proton
None, as water is neutral and cannot donate
H₂O, as it donates a proton to NH₃

questions.explanation: In the forward reaction H₂O loses H⁺ (becoming OH⁻) and NH₃ gains it (becoming NH₄⁺). The proton donor, H₂O, is the Brønsted–Lowry acid; NH₃ is the base.

questions.stem: Which pair of species is a conjugate acid–base pair?

options.text: H₃PO₄ and HPO₄²⁻
CH₃COOH and NH₃
H₂PO₄⁻ and HPO₄²⁻
HSO₄⁻ and SO₄⁻

questions.explanation: The two species differ by exactly one proton: H₂PO₄⁻ − H⁺ = HPO₄²⁻. One H fewer and a charge one unit more negative is the signature of a conjugate pair.

questions.stem:
Dihydrogenphosphate ions react with ammonia:
H₂PO₄⁻(aq) + NH₃(aq) ⇌ HPO₄²⁻(aq) + NH₄⁺(aq)
Which statement describes the role of H₂PO₄⁻ in the forward reaction?

options.text: It is an acid, as it gives up a proton to NH₃
It is a base, as it loses a proton to NH₃
It is a base, since negative ions only accept H⁺
It is both an acid and a base in this reaction

questions.explanation: H₂PO₄⁻ becomes HPO₄²⁻: it loses H⁺, which NH₃ accepts. So in this reaction H₂PO₄⁻ is a Brønsted–Lowry acid. With a stronger acid such as H₃O⁺, the same ion would act as a base.

questions.stem: Copper(II) oxide, CuO, is insoluble in water. It reacts with dilute sulfuric acid to form copper(II) sulfate and water. How should copper(II) oxide be classified?

options.text: As an alkali, as it neutralizes an acid
As a base, but it is not an alkali
As neither, as it contains no OH⁻ ions
As neither, since it is insoluble in water

questions.explanation: CuO accepts protons from the acid (O²⁻ + 2H⁺ → H₂O), so it is a base. An alkali is a base that dissolves in water to release OH⁻(aq); CuO is insoluble, so it is not an alkali.

questions.stem: What is the formula of the conjugate base of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH?

options.text: CH₃COO
CH₃COO⁻
CH₃COOH₂⁺
CH₂COOH⁻

questions.explanation: The conjugate base is formed when the acid donates one proton, H⁺. Ethanoic acid loses the hydrogen of its –COOH group, so the formula loses one H and the charge falls by one: CH₃COOH → CH₃COO⁻ (the ethanoate ion).

questions.stem: Which is a correct equation for HCO₃⁻ acting as a Brønsted–Lowry base in the forward reaction?

options.text: HCO₃⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq) ⇌ H₂CO₃⁻(aq) + H₂O(l)
HCO₃⁻(aq) + OH⁻(aq) ⇌ CO₃²⁻(aq) + H₂O(l)
H₂CO₃(aq) + CH₃COO⁻(aq) ⇌ HCO₃⁻(aq) + CH₃COOH(aq)
HCO₃⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq) ⇌ H₂CO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

questions.explanation: HCO₃⁻ gains a proton from H₃O⁺, becoming H₂CO₃: gaining H⁺ is what a Brønsted–Lowry base does. Its charge rises by one, from −1 to 0, and the equation balances in atoms and charge.
